chapter: Rhythm Club, studio dates and the 1930s big bands
title: Playing head arrangements with his own band, "Mr. Bear"
summary: On a 1956 tour his band's best numbers were head arrangements that puzzled a rival band wanting to see the charts.

story.theme_name: Writing and arranging: how musicians compose
story.community_name: Writing, arranging and composing: how the music gets made

blocks.x: Especially Frankie Newton (inaudible). I had heard (inaudible) arrangements on things, man, (inaudible). I remember one time when I was travelling with my band, "Mr. Bear," in '56. We went in -- I had Horsecollar on the piano, two great guitar players and rhythm section.
S. & S. REPORTING COMPANY, INC. WOrth 2-2915 WOrth 2-2943

And everything we had was a rhythm -- Everything we played on that tour outside of some of those melodies -- some of the introduction things I play. Things we had gotten together -- you know, a little few arrangements, or something like that.
But the dramatic things that -- the things that're outstanding things that we would rock the hall with were head arrangements. We had no head arrangements.

We walk in this little town, this little band was there. And they invited us -- They was gonna gig too. And they was gonna (inaudible) run us off (inaudible) music. They went to see the (inaudible) guys say, "Where's the music? I'd like the see the arrangements to that."
I ain't got no arrangements. It's all head, man, you know. Put it together just like that.
